title: Open Waterway Designer document (.owd), format 0.5
description: One screening study of one river reach for one vessel: its inputs, the choices made and the results of each stage. Each stage records a hash of what it depended on; a stage whose hash no longer matches is stale. Numbers are SI. Geometry is GeoJSON in the project CRS.

format_version.description: The string "0.5" since spec 0017 ticket 6 (one design line per run). A 0.4 file opens and is saved as 0.5: its rolling-circle option (or the first other one) becomes the design line, its pool-lattice option the optimise stage's refined line, any other option is not kept, and its stages after sizing are marked stale. A file with the number 3 (format 0.3, spec 0007) opens the same way. An older file is refused, with no migration: rebuild the design.

crs.description: The project CRS: WGS84 / UTM. Null until the first import.

source_crs.description: The CRS each input came in, by input name, as EPSG:nnnn.

waterway_reaches.description: Reaches of the river by chainage on its centreline (spec 0007), in chainage order, not overlapping. Each has a waterway kind and the reduced-radius claim; stations take the inputs of the reach their projection falls in. Chainage not covered, or no reach at all, is a free-flowing river with no claim. `end_m` null runs to the end of the river.

reduced_radius_claim.description: `yes` only where the user claims the reduced GB 50139 radius, and only on a canal reach.

dem.description: The DEM is referenced, never embedded: path relative to the document, SHA-256 of the file (or, for a large sectioned file, its quick check: length and a hash of its structure and a sample of its blocks), its CRS and nodata value.

quick_check.description: COG-1: a tiled GeoTIFF of 64 MiB or more is recorded by its length and the SHA-256 of its header, its directories and every value they point to, and the stored bytes of a sample of blocks (every block of an image of 64 or fewer, else 32 spaced evenly). It misses a change made in place to a block it does not sample; `owd project status --full` hashes every byte.

holds_bathymetry.description: As for a DEM recorded by its SHA-256.

The user marks the DEM as holding the river bed below the water level (surveyed bathymetry), #363. With it and a water level, `fits` reads the depth from the DEM. Not checked by OWD; a new DEM clears it.

source.description: Where a fetched DEM came from (`owd fetch-dem`): the dataset, its licence notice, and each tile with its file, SHA-256, size and URL.

bed_model.description: Spec 0012: the bed of the river where there is no survey, from a depth profile. Inside the water, bed = water level - depth x shape. The depth is read along the river centreline from `points` of [river chainage in metres, depth in metres], linear between points and flat beyond the first and last; the shape is a parabola across the water, 1 at the centreline and 0 at the banks. Outside the water the DEM is read as before. The depth is assumed, not measured: every output that used it says so. A survey later replaces it. Optional.

season.description: The season the depths hold for, for example `dry`. Free text.

water_level.description: The water level as a profile along the river centreline (ADR 0006): points of [river chainage in metres, level in metres], read linearly between points and held flat beyond the first and last. Two points at one chainage make a step. A design line's station takes its level by projecting onto the river centreline. Optional: a document made before the profile has none.

seed_legs.description: Spec 0005: ordered lines joined into one design line before the rolling circle (`join_legs`). Optional.

banks.description: What the bank source says about the banks (draft ADR 0016, banks are a dataset): who made them, how accurate they are, and where the source is unsure. The bank lines stay in left_bank and right_bank. Optional; no member is required.

source.description: Who made the banks: a file the user gave, an edit in the app, or a bank source.

accuracy_m.description: The accuracy of the bank lines in metres, as the source states it; null when unknown.

low_confidence.description: Stretches of river chainage, in metres, where the source is unsure of the banks.

mouth.description: Spec 0017: the river mouth, where chainage 0 is. `point` is the first point of the stored centreline, in the project CRS: the river lines are stored running from it, and every river chainage (the water level, the bed depths, the waterway reaches, the low-confidence stretches) counts from it. `stated_as` says whether the user gave the point or said `downstream` (the lower end, by the water level or the ground). Null or absent: no mouth is stated, and chainage runs from the first point of the stored centreline.

run.description: Spec 0017 ticket 11: the run inputs (`schema/stages/inputs.run.1.schema.json`). `objective`: one design measure to minimise or maximise. `limits`: design measures each with a bound, at most one bound of each kind on a measure; a bound on cost is money and names its currency, a bound on another measure is in that measure's unit (m³ for the cuts, m² for land take, m for line length, a count of structures) and names none; a bound on capacity is refused until its unit is settled. `target_level`: the output level the run aims at. Every part is optional. Absent: no objective, no limits, and the target is concept. Nothing optimises on them yet.

rates.description: Spec 0017 ticket 12: the rates table (`schema/stages/inputs.rates.1.schema.json`): one rate per item, each an amount and a currency, all in one currency: dredge and dry cut per m³, disposal per m³ of all cut, haul per m³ per km. `haul_km` is the run's haul distance; `haul_by_reach` gives stretches of design-line chainage their own. A rate left out is refused when the cost is worked out, never read as zero. Absent: no cost.

buildings.description: BLD-1: a buildings file (GeoJSON Polygons or Points, WGS84 or WGS84 / UTM), referenced like the DEM and never embedded: path relative to the document, SHA-256, the number of buildings and the source CRS. `min_confidence` (0 to 1): a building below it is counted apart and never costed; `min_area_m2`: likewise for a smaller building; `near_cut_m`: the distance within which a building is reported as near the cut. Absent: no buildings.

points_of_interest.description: BLD-1: a points of interest file (GeoJSON Points, or Polygons and LineStrings labelled at a representative point; properties `name` and `kind`), referenced like the DEM and never embedded. Absent: none.

settlements.description: BLD-1: a settlements file (GeoJSON Polygons), referenced like the DEM and never embedded. Absent: none.

constraints.description: Spec 0017 ticket 13: the run's constraints (`schema/stages/inputs.constraints.1.schema.json`). `no_go`: polygons in the project CRS (an outer ring and holes, each a list of [x, y] points), each with a unique name and a kind; the re-route treats them as impassable and every design line reports those it touches. `cut_rate_multiplier`: a raster referenced like the DEM (path relative to the document, SHA-256, CRS, nodata), whose cell value multiplies the cut rate in that cell; no data means 1. Absent: no constraints.

fixed.description: Spec 0005: pieces the joined line must hold exactly. A pose is a point and a heading in degrees counter-clockwise from the project CRS's +x (east) axis. Optional.

reference_line.description: Spec 0016 T1, spec 0017 ticket 7: the reference line, one smooth line in the water that belongs to no vessel, as a stage record (`schema/stages/reference_line.1.schema.json`): the parameters as `settings`, the line, its low-confidence and outside-water stretches and notes as `results` (chainage along the line from its start), and as `depends_on` the hash of its whole input and the project CRS. The results' `line_basis` is the hash of what shapes the line (the banks, the river polygon, the project CRS and the parameters; the formula used before it was a stage): the bed is centred on the line while it matches. Not a stage of the chain: never rerun by `run`, and no design stage reads it. A file that holds it as `inputs.reference_line` opens with it moved here, keeping its hash, so a fresh line stays fresh. Optional.

water.description: Spec 0017 ticket 8: the water level along the design line, as a stage record (`schema/stages/water.1.schema.json`): the step between points as `settings`, the points (design-line chainage, the river chainage each was read at, the level, where it comes from: given, pool or open river, a pool's minimum and maximum level when it has them, and whether it is held flat beyond the profile's ends) and the stretches as `results`, and as `depends_on` the hash of the input it read. Not a stage of the chain: the volumes stage runs it, and no other stage's hash reads it. Optional.

plan_cut.description: Ticket C2b: the plan cut of the design line, the fairway at the water surface less the river polygon (`owd plan-cut`). Plan only: no terrain, no water level. Not a stage of the chain: never rerun by `run`, stale when the river, its banks or centreline, the CRS, the sizing, the design line or the settings change. Optional.

envelope.description: Spec 0016 T2: the largest vessel the river allows, a sweep of single-hull sizes on the reference line (`owd envelope`). Not a stage of the chain: never rerun by `run`, stale when the banks, the river polygon, the reference line, the custom vessel or the settings change. Optional.

fits.description: The answer to "what fits" over every vessel class (spec 0012). It is not a stage: it never reruns by itself, and it shows as stale when the banks or the centreline change.

reach.description: Spec 0012: the reach the study was started from. Start, end and via points and the trace are the user's own longitude-latitude clicks. The route is OSM way ids only, never OSM geometry (ODbL); a stretch with no waterway near it is kept as the user drew it, kind `as-drawn`. Optional.

low_confidence_width.description: Spec 0012: stretches of the generated banks where the water was too narrow to trust (under `min_width_m`) or was not found; spec 0013 adds stretches where a bank check failed (`repaired`). Chainage is along the generated centreline, in metres from its start. Optional.

checks.description: Spec 0013, kind `repaired`: the bank checks that failed. `side`, `missing`, `jump`, `excursion` and `width-wide` were repaired; `width-narrow` and `crossing` (the banks still cross after the repairs) are flagged and the banks kept.

provenance.description: Spec 0012: where each generated input came from, by input name. Optional: a document with none gives the same results. Each record names its source (an `owd-reach` registry id), its date, the licence notice that travels into every export, and a mark: `default` (made by OWD), `edited` (a default the user changed) or `user` (the user's own).

design_measure.description: Spec 0017: one quantity of the whole design.

provisional.description: True while the default behind this input is not yet calibrated (spec 0012).

settings.description: The parameters the input was made with (for example the JRC mask threshold), so a reviewer can see which choices are provisional defaults.

line_stretch.description: A stretch of a line by chainage (m), with its kind when it has one.

settings.description: The method that makes the one design line (`method`), the settings of each method by method name, and the line the user gave (`given`) for the method `given`. A setting left out takes its default.

method.description: Spec 0017: the method that makes the one design line. Default rolling_circle. `river_following` is the river-following line (OPT-4).

given.description: Ticket C21: the line the user gave, for the method `given`: its name and its points in the project CRS.

use_water.description: Spec 0005: the water-aware rolling circle. Null (the default) means on when the inputs have a river polygon. A version 1 document records false when it opens, so its results do not change.

clearance_m.description: Spec 0005: clearance from the bank, metres, added to half the bottom width when the water is shrunk to navigable water. Default 0.

r_pref_m.description: Spec 0005: a preferred radius for the fairway fit, metres; bends tighter than it are penalised, never refused. Default none.

fairness_weight.description: Weight on the squared change of heading between stations in the least-cost re-route (spec 0005). 0, the default, gives the re-route without it.

results.description: Spec 0017: the one design line (`schema/stages/alignment.1.schema.json`): its line from the mouth, its method and settings, its checks, its bends and its cut-offs. Null until the stage has run.

rule_sets.description: The selected Rule Sets (spec 0007), in selection order. `owd` is always selected. `source` says whether the user chose the set (`typed`) or the tool did (`default`).

set_inputs.description: The inputs the selected sets apply on, such as `se_quality`, each with its source.

custom_vessel.description: A custom vessel (spec 0015): the user's own dimensions, sized like a catalogue class. When it is set, `vessel_standard_id` is null. For a convoy, the length and beam are those of the whole convoy; `n_abreast` and `n_in_line` are for a convoy only. `gb_class` is the GB 50139 channel class, read by GB 50139 alone. `air_draught_m` and `deadweight_t` are stored only.

rule_sets.description: The Rule Set selection as words, such as `pianc-wg141@0.3.0 (se_quality B)`.
